(Institute for the Study of War — Iran Update Special Report, July 17, 2026. Retrieved via WebFetch; condensed by fetch tool.)

Strategic Strikes and Infrastructure Targeting
The United States struck several bridges and railroads in southern Iran to disrupt supply routes to Bandar Abbas, Hormozgan Province. The U.S. also targeted the Radio and Communications Regulatory Authority's office in Bandar Abbas on July 16, along with the city's railway junction station approximately 10 kilometers west of the city.
Bandar Abbas hosts the IRGC Navy First Naval District and numerous naval facilities. The Shahid Rajaei Port handles roughly 85 percent of Iran's container traffic and connects to Iran's national rail and highway networks.

Iranian Retaliatory Actions
Iran struck critical infrastructure in Kuwait on July 17, damaging several power generation units at an unspecified power and water desalination plant. The Kuwaiti Electricity, Water, and Renewable Energy Ministry attributed the attack to "Iranian aggression."
Iran attacked US targets in Bahrain, Jordan, Qatar, and Oman on July 16-17. The IRGC Navy claimed it destroyed a naval surveillance radar on the Salamah Archipelago and an air surveillance radar near Ghanem Island.
Iran also attacked a former US base in Syria on July 17, with the IRGC stating it targeted "a US special operations command center at al Tanf Garrison" in retaliation for killing of Iranian soldiers in Iranshahr.

Maritime Disruption
Iran targeted a Thai-flagged vessel in the Strait of Hormuz on July 17. Tasnim News Agency claimed the IRGC Navy struck the vessel after it "ignored warnings" and attempted transit "without Iranian authorization."
Only eight vessels transited through the strait on July 16, demonstrating how Iranian attacks deter shipping companies from using the route.
